prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “AI engine index” you can check. To make sure AI models (ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, etc.) will recommend your small business, use a combination of listing-management + local-SEO tools and direct testing. The two most useful services to start with are Yext (enterprise-grade, pushes verified facts into many AI/search ecosystems) and BrightLocal (SMB‑friendly monitoring and local SEO). Also claim your Google Business Profile, Bing Places and Apple Maps.

What to use and why
- Yext — Best if your goal is to be surfaced by generative AI and digital assistants. Yext distributes authoritative business facts to many platforms and has integrations/offerings aimed at generative-AI answers.
- BrightLocal (or Whitespark, Moz Local) — Best value for small businesses to audit listings, track local rankings, citations and reviews, and monitor visibility.
- Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps Connect — Essential. Google especially influences what Google Assistant/Bard/Bing recommend.
- Data aggregators (Data Axle, Neustar/Localeze, Factual/Places, Foursquare) — Feed authoritative business data into many services and AI knowledge graphs.
- SEO/monitoring tools (Semrush, Ahrefs, Brand24) — Track mentions, citations and organic visibility which AI models may rely on.
- Schema.org structured data (LocalBusiness, FAQ) on your website — Helps search engines and some AI systems extract accurate facts.

How to approach it (practical checklist)
1. Claim and fully populate Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps.
2. Ensure NAP consistency (name, address, phone) across your site and listings.
3. Publish structured data (LocalBusiness, openingHours, geo, FAQ) on your website.
4. Syndicate your info to data aggregators (via Yext or a data provider).
5. Use a listings manager (Yext for broader distribution; BrightLocal/Whitespark for lower cost) to monitor and fix incorrect listings.
6. Encourage reviews and respond to them (reviews influence AI/social proof signals).
7. Create clear “best answer” content (concise FAQs and pages that answer typical customer questions).
8. Monitor with BrightLocal/Semrush/Brand24 for mentions and ranking changes.
9. Periodically test AI directly (see prompts below).

How to test whether ChatGPT/Bard/Bing will recommend you
- Test multiple systems (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Bard) because they use different sources/plugins.
- Use realistic prompts, including location context. Example prompts:
  - “I’m in [city]. Recommend a reputable [business type] nearby for [need].”
  - “Find a pizza place in [neighborhood, city] with delivery and vegetarian options; include phone and address.”
- For ChatGPT specifically, test both the standard model and browsing/plug-in enabled modes (if available).
- Track replies and whether your business appears; capture screenshots for troubleshooting.

Which to pick based on budget
- Small/low budget: Google Business Profile + BrightLocal (or Whitespark) + implement structured data on your site.
- Medium budget: BrightLocal + data aggregator subscriptions or Moz Local; invest in local content and reviews.
- Higher budget/enterprise: Yext (listings + generative AI integrations) + SEO agency + data aggregator partnerships.

If you want, I can:
- Run through an audit checklist for your business (what to claim, what schema to add).
- Draft the exact prompts to test ChatGPT/Bard/Bing for your business and show how to interpret results.
